name: Gambia
fact: Renowned as a vibrant birdwatching paradise, Gambia provides vital habitat to more than five hundred avian species along the scenic waterway of the Gambia River.

name: Ghana
fact: Kakum National Park features a celebrated canopy walkway suspended forty meters above the forest floor, offering visitors spectacular panoramic views of untouched tropical rainforest.

name: Guinea
fact: Rising dramatically across the highlands, the Fouta Djallon plateau forms West Africa's primary water tower, feeding the headwaters of the iconic Niger and Senegal rivers.

name: Guinea-Bissau
fact: The lush Bijagós Archipelago encompasses eighty-eight islands designated as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, famous for rare saltwater hippopotamuses and thriving marine turtle nesting sanctuaries.

name: Kenya
fact: Generating approximately ninety percent of its electricity from geothermal steam, wind, and solar installations, Kenya stands as a global champion of clean renewable energy.

name: Lesotho
fact: Perched high in the Maloti Mountains, Lesotho is the only sovereign country in the world situated entirely above fourteen hundred meters in altitude.

name: Liberia
fact: Dense tropical wilderness within Sapo National Park safeguards one of West Africa's last primary rainforests, providing vital protection for endangered pygmy hippos.

name: Libya
fact: Along the Mediterranean coast, the UNESCO World Heritage site of Leptis Magna preserves magnificent Roman architectural treasures, including an imposing amphitheater and ornate marble temples.

name: Madagascar
fact: Spectacular century-old trees frame the famous Avenue of the Baobabs, creating one of the world's most iconic and enchanting natural landscapes.

name: Malawi
fact: Lake Malawi National Park protects an unparalleled aquatic ecosystem harboring hundreds of brilliantly colored cichlid fish species found nowhere else on the planet.

name: Mali
fact: Constructed entirely from sun-baked earthen bricks, the Great Mosque of Djenné stands as the largest adobe architectural masterpiece on Earth and a treasured UNESCO site.

name: Mauritania
fact: Visible even to astronauts orbiting Earth, the enormous Richat Structure forms a mesmerizing circular geological formation across the Mauritanian Sahara.

name: Mauritius
fact: At Chamarel, natural dunes display seven distinct colors of volcanic sands that magically settle into vibrant stratified bands under the tropical sun.

name: Morocco
fact: Founded in 859 AD in Fez, the University of al-Qarawiyyin holds the distinction of being the world's oldest continually operating institution of higher learning.

name: Mozambique
fact: Pristine coastal waters surrounding the Bazaruto Archipelago safeguard East Africa's largest viable population of rare dugongs alongside vibrant coral reefs.

name: Namibia
fact: Namibia was the first African nation to write environmental protection directly into its constitution, fostering community conservancies that allow wildlife populations to flourish.
